title: File Processing and Exception Handling
overview: This topic is practical programming: robustly process files and handle runtime exceptions. You need correct read/write/append behaviour, serial/sequential/random-file processing, and exception handling that responds to expected failures without hiding ordinary programming errors.
syllabusPoints: Open and close files in read, write and append modes.
Read records from and write records to files.
Process serial, sequential and random files correctly.
Explain exceptions and when exception handling is appropriate.
Write program code that handles specified exceptions and recovers or terminates cleanly.

definitions.definition: A runtime event/error condition that interrupts normal execution and may be caught by a handler.
Opens a file to inspect existing contents without intentionally replacing them.
Opens a file for output, typically creating/replacing contents depending on language/API.
Adds new data after existing contents.
Code executed when a specified exception occurs.

sections.title: File lifecycle
content: Open the file using the mode that matches the task, perform operations, and ensure resources are closed even if a failure occurs. Wrong mode choice can erase data or make required updates impossible.

sections.title: Serial and sequential processing
content: Read records one at a time until end-of-file. Serial files are processed in stored arrival order; sequential files exploit key order for tasks such as merges or ordered reports.

sections.title: Random file processing
content: Use a record number/address, often derived from a key/hash, to seek directly to the target record. Updates and retrieval must use exactly the same organisation, record-size/addressing and collision conventions used when the file was created.

sections.title: Exception handling
content: Handle failures that can reasonably occur at runtime: missing file, permission failure, invalid conversion, unavailable resource, etc. A handler might report the issue, retry, use a safe fallback or terminate cleanly.

examples.label: Worked example

sections.title: Exceptions versus validation
content: Exception handling is not a replacement for normal conditions/validation. If a value can be checked normally before an operation, an IF may be clearer; exceptions are for exceptional runtime situations that interrupt the normal path.

examTips: Paper 4 allows Python, Java or Visual Basic console programming—know exact syntax for your chosen language.
Name the exception/condition and the recovery action.
Ensure files are closed/cleaned up after use.
commonMistakes: Opening in write mode when the task says preserve and append.
Catching every exception and doing nothing.
Using exceptions instead of ordinary validation for every branch.
